extracted.intended_audience: practitioners, applicants, and officers dealing with Patents, Designs and Trade Marks under the Patents, Designs and Trade Marks Act 1883 (UK)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements, evidentiary effects, and remedies governing patent, design and trade mark applications, oppositions, registrations, infringements, renewals, extensions, and associated documents under the 1883 Act (UK).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings (Patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: When required; when sufficient; size of original drawing; copy drawings; drawings for Illustrated Journal; absence of a scale an imperfection; drawings may explain an ambiguity; examiner reports on drawings; Rules and Instructions as to drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original and copy drawings must meet prescribed size requirements; a missing scale is an imperfection; drawings can be used to clarify ambiguities in the specification; examiners report on adequacy; follow the Patent Rules and Instructions (see pp. 8, 9, 164–180).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings (Designs)
rubrics_metrics.description: A drawing of the Design must accompany the application; three copy drawings are also to be sent; size requirements; instead of drawings, tracings, photographs, specimens or representations may be sent; drawings may be refused where not suitable; Rules and Instructions as to drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the required number and size of drawings (see pp. 73–74, 210, 220). If drawings are unsuitable, the application may be refused; alternative representational media are acceptable subject to Rules (Designs Rules and Instructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings (Trade Marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings or representations to accompany Trade Mark applications; rules as to number, size, and where marks are large; drawings for Illustrated Journal; Rules and Instructions as to drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the number and size of representations required by the Trade Mark Rules (see pp. 86–87, 236–258). Large marks have special presentation requirements for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Specification (Patent)
rubrics_metrics.description: May accompany the application; requires no stamp; must include a title and indicate the nature of the invention; draws examiner attention to title; must not vary from the rest of the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional spec can be used to secure priority/provisional protection on filing (form at p. 191). Ensure title is accurate (examiner reports on title) and the provisional does not conflict with any later complete specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete Specification (Patent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete specification must particularly describe and ascertain the nature of the invention; when left it is referred to the Examiner; it may be amended; acceptance of the complete specification gives further protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare complete specification to satisfy description/ascertainment requirements (see pp. 13–16). Amendments are permitted subject to Rules; Examiner reviews completeness and identity with any provisional specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Formalities (Patent)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for a patent must be accompanied by a declaration and a specification; application is referred to an Examiner; title must indicate the object of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File the required declaration and provisional/complete specification, include a clear title indicating the invention's object; follow prescribed Patent forms and Rules (see pp. 3–10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners — scope, reports and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners appointed by the Board of Trade report on whether the invention is fairly described, whether the application/specifications are properly prepared, whether the title indicates the subject-matter, and whether two applications comprise the same invention; reports are not published or open to public inspection and are not normally producible in legal proceedings except on appeal to the law officer or by order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners' reports influence acceptance/amendments (see pp. 9–15). Treat examiner reports as confidential internal reports; they can be relied on administratively but have limited disclosure in litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Protection / Publication on Acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of an application produces provisional protection and publication of the invention; acceptance of a complete specification produces further protection; publication is the date from which certain effects run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing and acceptance trigger differing levels of protection (provisional vs. protection from complete specification). Publication upon acceptance has evidentiary and timing consequences (see pp. 23–24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealing, Date and Time Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Sealing of Letters Patent has temporal effects (date/time of sealing matters); death of applicant before sealing has specified consequences; sealing must be registered and entries made in register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sealing marks formal grant; various procedures (notice, registration) and consequences (rights, transfers) depend on sealing date (see pp. 20–22, 35–36, 59).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of Patent — grounds and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds for extension include: (1) nature and merits of the invention regarding the public (amount of utility required, success, benefit), (2) profits made by patentee (all resulting profits, manufacturer's profits, deductions), and (3) other circumstances (personal merit of inventor, effect of importation, assignee standing, inutility, effect on the public, granting of licences). Term of extension generally not exceeding 7 years (14 in special cases); conditions may be imposed (e.g., annuity, share of profits, fixed price sale, Crown use, disclaimers). Petition practice, timing and forms described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions for extension must be presented six months before expiration, follow prescribed form and procedure, may be advertised and opposed, and are referred to Judicial Committee; consider public interest and accounting for profits when seeking extension (see pp. 37–46).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlargement of Time for Renewal or Procedural Acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Enlargement of time may be granted for taking out certificate of renewal or for doing acts/taking proceedings in Patents, Designs and Trade Marks; conditions apply; not to exceed three months; fees payable; infringement during enlarged time addressed; forms and required statements in application prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply using the prescribed form (see pp. 25, 168, 200); note the three-month cap and fee requirements; consider risk of infringement during extended period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate Patent where Original Lost
rubrics_metrics.description: A duplicate patent may be granted where the original is lost; there is a prescribed form of application and fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified form and pay the fee for duplicate issuance (see pp. 60, 203).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition of Inventions and Unregistered Designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions may be exhibited before grant only at industrial or international exhibitions certified by the Board of Trade and under conditions; unregistered designs exhibited at such exhibitions (or published/described during the holding) will not invalidate subsequent registration provided the exhibition is certified, notice given to the Comptroller, and registration application is made within six months of the opening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certify exhibitions with the Board of Trade and give notice to the Comptroller using prescribed forms (see pp. 61, 80–81, 216, 231); comply with conditions to preserve later registrability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright in a Design — duration and searching
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence of copyright in a design continues for five years; searches can be made as to existence; there is a prescribed form for request and a fee for search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed search form and pay fee to determine existing copyright status before filing (see pp. 75–78, 222).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Registration of Designs Abolished
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional registration of designs has been abolished by the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on provisional registration procedures; proceed with full application and accompanying representations/drawings (see p. 71).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of Designs — who, class and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Who can register (proprietor); registration must be for a particular class of goods; classes of goods prescribed; where a design is contrary to law or morality it cannot be registered; registration confers copyright for five years and remedies for infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the correct class of goods; if in doubt Comptroller may determine class; ensure design is lawful and moral for registrability; registration grants statutory rights and remedies (see pp. 70–75, 80–81, 212–215, 233).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of Trade Marks — classes, restrictions and renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade Mark registration must be for a class (or part) of goods; identical marks on register not to be registered (unless for a different class or by court order); restrictions: marks calculated to deceive, misrepresentation, false statements, or contrary to law/morality are not registrable; renewal required every fourteen years with prescribed fees and possible restoration if removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the class of goods in the application; expect oppositions on identity/consumer deception grounds; pay renewal fees on time or risk removal and additional fees for restoration (see pp. 95–103, 111–113, 240–242, 289).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marks not registrable as New Trade Marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain marks (e.g., the Royal Arms; certain words like 'Registered', 'Copyright', 'Patented'; initials except combined with other matter) are not to be registered as new trade marks and may only be registered as old marks in limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid attempting to register prohibited words/symbols as new marks; consult Rules/Instructions regarding 'old marks' classification (see pp. 90–93, 259–260).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Registration — evidence of exclusive user
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration is primafacie evidence of the right to exclusive user of a Trade Mark; it becomes conclusive evidence after five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration creates strong evidentiary presumption for enforcement; however, subject to any rights appearing on the register and the condition that the mark was properly registrable (see pp. 102–103).

rubrics_metrics.name: Goodwill and Trade Mark Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: A Trade Mark attaches to the goodwill of the business concerned in the registered class of goods; it is assignable only with the goodwill; assignment of goodwill assigns the mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure assignments include the associated goodwill and are registered to retain enforceable rights; consult forms and register-entry requirements (see pp. 98, 123).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition Procedures (Patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition to grant of a patent: grounds include invention obtained from opponent/employee/representative, invention already patented, or identity with prior application; persons who may oppose; notice must be given within prescribed time (e.g., two months from advertisement), must state grounds, include an address for service and an unstamped duplicate; Comptroller notifies applicant; evidence and hearing rules apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File opposition in prescribed form within time limits (see pp. 16–20, 165–170, forms at pp. 192–195); expect examination, possibility of appeal to law officer, and that opposition affects sealing/time of sealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition Procedures (Trade Marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition to registration of a Trade Mark must be given in prescribed form and time; must be in duplicate, state grounds, be accompanied by an unstamped copy, include address for service; security for costs by opponent may be required; counterstatement by applicant; disputes can be brought before the Court and certain procedural steps and forms apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Trade Mark Rules for opposition, security for costs, and Court procedures (see pp. 96–98, 240–241, forms at pp. 273, 286–287).

rubrics_metrics.name: Licences — compulsory and ordinary
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory licences: Board of Trade may order grant (only for patents granted on applications made after 31 Dec 1883), application/grounds/practice described, orders enforceable by mandamus; ordinary licences: must be registered, prescribed form of application and accompanying original licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compulsory licence petitions follow a specific procedure with forms and possible opposition (see pp. 33–35, 170–171, forms at pp. 197–198, 202). Register ordinary licences to preserve rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of a Patent — procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Revocation is now obtained by petition to the Court (sce revocation by scire facias abolished); who may present petition, particulars of objections, amendment opportunities, burden/order of pleading at hearing; order of revocation to be entered on the register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring petitions following prescribed practice; be aware of remedies if revocation for fraud (possible grant of new patent) and registration/entry consequences (see pp. 41–46).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for Infringing Trade Marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil remedies include actions for infringement (registration/certificate preconditions for new marks), injunctions (interlocutory relief possible), discovery, accounts (limited to six years' profits), and damages (nominal or substantial); criminal remedies under Merchandise Marks Act and offences like forgery and false pretences also apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose appropriate remedy (injunction, account, damages, or criminal prosecution) and follow Rules of Supreme Court for interlocutory relief and pleadings; be mindful of defences, effect of delay, and statutory limits (see pp. 104–108, 106–107, 108–110).

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunctions and Interim Relief (Patent and Trade Mark actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interlocutory injunctions may be obtained ex parte but are usually on notice; notice of motion and evidence requirements specified; Rules of Supreme Court govern practice; inspection and discovery may be ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply under Rules (Orders xxii, xxxiii, xxxiv etc.) with supporting evidence; ex parte orders exceptional — typically notice and evidence are required (see pp. 52–56, 106).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registers — entries, inspection and evidentiary status
rubrics_metrics.description: Registers of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks are maintained under the Act: names/addresses of proprietors, assignments, licences, extensions, revocations and other particulars are entered; registers are primafacie evidence of matters entered; certified/sealed copies and Comptroller certificates are receivable in evidence; inspection hours prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure accurate register entries to secure evidentiary benefits; obtain certified extracts where required for litigation; correct clerical errors promptly (see pp. 35, 79, 110, 122–125, 171–174, 212–215, 241–245).

rubrics_metrics.name: Falsification of Register Entries — offence and penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Making false entries or false copies of entries in registers, or tendering false copies in evidence, is a misdemeanour and punishable; other related offences (forgery under Merchandise Marks Act) are provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain integrity of register submissions; falsification carries criminal consequences (see pp. 127–129, 108).

rubrics_metrics.name: Models (Patents) — requirement and payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Models of patented inventions may be required by the Science and Art Department or Patent Museum; payment for models in disputes to be settled by Board of Trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide models when requested and be prepared for Board of Trade adjudication on compensation (see pp. 64–66).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Applications and its Consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of the invention occurs on acceptance of application; publication of a complete specification occurs on acceptance; publication may affect infringement timing and prior user questions; descriptions published during exhibitions may not prejudice subsequent registration if conditions met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand timing of publication relative to rights and enforceability; plan filings around exhibitions and publications to preserve rights (see pp. 22–24, 61, 80–81).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees — payment, forms, and Board of Trade powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees are payable for patents, designs and trade marks; fees to be paid by stamped forms; Board of Trade (with Treasury sanction) may prescribe or reduce fees; forms and certificates of payment are prescribed; notices issued where annual fees are paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prescribed stamped forms and certificates; monitor fee schedules and deadlines (renewals, annual fees) to avoid removal or loss of rights (see pp. 25, 37, 153–184, 217–222, 262–266).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence — seals, certified copies and Comptroller certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Seal of the Patent Office is to be judicially noticed; certified and sealed copies of documents in the Patent Office are receivable in evidence; registers are primafacie evidence; a certificate of the Comptroller is receivable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on certified copies and Comptroller's certificates as admissible evidence; be aware of the procedural steps to obtain certified documents (see pp. 121–125, 130–133).
